newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street rallies on retail data, tech stocks lag.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street rallies on retail data, tech stocks lag.

text.p: Wall Street stocks jumped higher on Thursday, with weak May retail sales data helping to fuel the Dow to its fifth day of record highs.
Analysts said the weaker-than-expected data prompted a bond market rally that, in turn, spurred the stocks up to a high of about 7662 before scaling back to 7650, a 74-point increase.
But the high-technology stocks largely faltered, with the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite nearly unchanged at 1408.
"The market is making new highs but the technology sector is not part of the picture," said Arun Kumar, equities strategist at Lehman Brothers.
Analysts said the sector was weighed down by Intel Corp which was cut this morning by both Goldman Sachs and Cowen & Co. Intel shares slid about 3-1/2 to 144.
U.S. May retail sales dropped 0.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $210.3 billion after revised drops of 0.9 percent in April and 0.3 percent in March.
Wall Street economists had expected the May sales to increase 0.4 percent.
Jobless claims for the week ended June 7 edged up to 339,000. Economists had expected the claims number to fall.
The combined data, which suggests a slowdown in economic activity, made investors more confident that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates when it meets in early July.
Peggy Farley, managing director and chief executive of Amas Securities Inc, said the figures were a "good Fed comforter."
Analysts said it was the first time in more than 15 years that retail sales have weakened for three months in a row.
The benchmark 30-year bond surged to 27/32 at a 6.77 percent yield while the Standard & Poor's futures index was up 8.05 to 878.60.

Hildegard Zagorski, market analyst at Prudential Securities, said the stock market strength could be seen in several sectors, including banks, financial stocks as well as cyclical stocks like pulp and paper.
The bank index was up about almost 10 points, or 1.5 percent, to 644. Weyerhaeuser Co gained 7/8 to 54-1/4 and International Paper Co rose one to 51-3/8.

Polo Ralph Lauren RL.N strode into the market with a 5-1/4 gain, rising to 31-1/4, in its first day of trading. The design house's shares jumped about 25 percent at the opening of trading, one day after its intial public offering.

Philip Morris shares gained 2-1/4 to 44-7/8. The company was leading the tobacco industry's challenge to a Massachusetts law that requires the disclosure of cigarette ingredients to state health authorities.

On the Nasdaq, technology stocks fell under the pressure from chip giant Intel's stumble. Applied Materials Inc shares fell 1-1/2 to 60-3/8, 3Com Corp slipped 10/16 to 46-15/16 and Teleport Communications Group Inc shed 1/4 to 29-3/4.
Cisco Systems Inc lost one to 62-11/16.
